how: Short calls recruit participants to take a spot, brigade a forming letter, contribute clicks, and keep going.
A participant accepts the brigade directive with a bare assent.
The explicit brigade directive receives an unqualified agreement in its reply.
Participants propose a banner and gator, ask for a design, offer a quicker slogan, and direct enlargement for an alligator.
A proposer names a gator project and later reports starting its leftmost pixels.
Participants report starting pixels and having made something, without establishing a completed shared mark.
A reported peace offering identifies a repaired border pixel by its coordinates.
Public defence calls name a Florida logo and a reported attempt by Tenn to take the spot.
A visitor proposes mutual upkeep among neighbouring college logos, receiving personal assent and referral rather than a completed collective agreement.
A visitor greets the room, reports repairing a border pixel as a peace offering, and pursues contacts for prospective mutual upkeep.
A reported peace-offering pixel and prospective mutual upkeep warrant a gift and outreach, while completed reciprocal barter requires evidence this exchange does not supply.
Distinguish help initiating an agreement from help following one, since the border repair is already reported when the alliance is proposed.
A visitor carries a proposal between related venues and reports contacting another participant, without showing a formal mandate.
A member condemns the proposed conversion of a neighbour's logo without establishing that anyone stopped placing.
Two posts call for converting another college's logo, instantiating attack proposals without proving the proposed conversions occurred.
One attack proposal receives a bare negative judgement, while a parallel proposal receives enthusiastic assent.
A participant celebrates the ongoing work while urging others to continue.
A reply treats an offer of help as late after the placement deadline, minimally marking the event's end.
A proposed gator and a rally to gator nation express participation as an existing school body.
Treating joking shunning as decided order requires evidence of an enacted sanction, and these calls cannot establish either enforced organisation or its comprehensive absence.

statement: routing a proposal to the room doing the work
how: Members distinguish the school venue from the logo workers' venue and route an alliance proposal there while offering personal assent.
A traitor accusation elicits a call to shun without evidence identifying the alleged act or showing an enforced exclusion.

statement: tracking the placement wait without claiming a workaround
how: A participant monitors the placement interval without identifying any method for bypassing it.

statement: locating work through landmarks and directions
how: A forming coloured letter and a direction of enlargement guide contributors without supplying a pixel-by-pixel template.
An offer can become placement help only before the canvas deadline, while a later offer remains discussable and can be answered as too late.
Requests for extra clicks and a quicker design do not establish a judgement that the room cannot build or hold its work.
A banner call receives a report of making something, but the report does not establish that the call recruited its maker.
The initial proposal already calls for participation, preventing isolation of a distinct start causing a subsequent recruitment call.
Design requests and an alternative slogan do not reveal whether a shared template settled the design.
An unspecified claim of cheating does not identify scripts, bots, or spare accounts.
A new gator proposal and defence of an existing logo do not establish that building the former caused defence of the latter.
The defence call and unspecified cheating report supply no link from upkeep pressure to a machine workaround.
The traitor accusation does not reveal the alleged act, changed pixels, or motive.
Personal assent followed by referral to the working venue does not express a dispute over who can bind placers.
A proposed alliance and venue referral do not establish an agreement that prompted a dispute about binding members.
A proposal and reported outreach leave agreement between the operative groups unresolved.
Warning against expanding into defended work does not establish a guest building under a host's rule.
A reported takeover threat and defence request do not report loss or relocation.
The alliance proposal names neighbouring logos without saying defence pressure caused the negotiation.
The visitor explains cooperation through neighbouring logos rather than a documented shortage causing the host to request outside help.
Defence calls and a prospective alliance do not establish joining a coalition because of an attack.
The objection to converting a neighbour's logo does not invoke a settled border or deal.
The defence request establishes neither insufficient strength nor a resulting move.
Recruitment and subsequent conversion proposals appear in different threads without a passage connecting the recruitment to attacking.
The alliance proposal is not described as a response to an attack call.
The traitor exchange identifies no rival room, leaving external contest talk unresolved.
No passage connects the conversion proposals to the separate traitor exchange as a continuation of the same rival contest.
Cheering accompanies a continuing request for clicks without identifying a finished mark whose completion prompted it.
A late-help correction does not contest a cleaned canvas, retained version, or account of the group's history.
The reply to a late helper supplies no decision about preserving a group, mark, or relationship.
A celebration and later correction of a helper do not show that celebrating prompted preservation of a record.
The late-help exchange supplies no link from recording the event to deciding what to continue.
Referral to an existing logo-working venue supplies no evidence of flood complaints, posting rules, moderator containment, or opening a canvas subreddit.
The venue referral is explained by where logo work occurs rather than by a documented flood of recruitment posts.
A joking shunning reply alone does not establish that the host venue was keyed as an April Fools takeover or licence.
Naming another college's logo as a target does not document an inherited quarrel.
The attack and defence titles name colleges without explaining a pre-canvas rivalry as the reason for targeting.
